events.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.

Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.

## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)

Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).

Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:

- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.

- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
  as **memory**.

Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.

## Resuming after an interruption

State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:

- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

## Final report (your last message)

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.

## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)

There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
`subagents` skill):

- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.

Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.
I'll start by reading the existing AJCR Descent file and the AJC source files.

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Pullbacks
7	import Mathlib.FieldTheory.Galois.Basic
8	
9	/-!
10	# Semilinear actions on schemes
11	
12	This is the scheme-level action vocabulary used by finite-Galois descent.  It
13	matches the API of the quotient engine in the sibling Algebraic Jacobian
14	project so that engine can be ported without a parallel set of conventions.
15	
16	The inversion in `toSpecAut` is forced by contravariance of `Spec` and by the
17	group law on categorical automorphisms.  `SemilinearGalAction` then records an
18	action on a scheme whose structural morphism covers this action on the base.
19	
20	## Main declarations
21	
22	* `AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.toSpecAut`: the action induced on a spectrum.
23	* `AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.SemilinearGalAction`: a semilinear action on
24	  a scheme over a field extension.
25	* `SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen`: the exact geometric condition used
26	  by the scheme quotient construction.
27	-/
28	
29	set_option autoImplicit false
30	
31	universe u
32	
33	open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry
34	
35	namespace AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent
36	
37	section SpecAut
38	
39	variable (G : Type*) [Group G] (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
40	  [MulSemiringAction G A]
41	
42	lemma toRingHom_comp (gamma tau : G) :
43	    (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A gamma).comp
44	        (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A tau) =
45	      MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A (gamma * tau) :=
46	  RingHom.ext fun x => (mul_smul gamma tau x).symm
47	
48	lemma toRingHom_one :
49	    MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A (1 : G) = RingHom.id A :=
50	  RingHom.ext fun x => one_smul G x
51	
52	/-- A group acting on a commutative ring acts on its spectrum.  The inverse in
53	the ring action makes this a group homomorphism after contravariance of `Spec`.
54	-/
55	noncomputable def toSpecAut : G →* Aut (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) :=
56	  MonoidHom.mk'
57	    (fun gamma =>
58	      { hom := Spec.map
59	          (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A gamma⁻¹))
60	        inv := Spec.map
61	          (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A gamma))
62	        hom_inv_id := by
63	          rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, toRingHom_comp,
64	            inv_mul_cancel, toRingHom_one, CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id]
65	        inv_hom_id := by
66	          rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, toRingHom_comp,
67	            mul_inv_cancel, toRingHom_one, CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id] })
68	    (fun gamma tau => by
69	      refine Iso.ext ?_
70	      change Spec.map
71	          (CommRingCat.ofHom
72	            (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A (gamma * tau)⁻¹)) =
73	        Spec.map
74	            (CommRingCat.ofHom
75	              (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A tau⁻¹)) ≫
76	          Spec.map
77	            (CommRingCat.ofHom
78	              (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A gamma⁻¹))
79	      rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, toRingHom_comp,
80	        ← mul_inv_rev])
81	
82	lemma toSpecAut_hom (gamma : G) :
83	    (toSpecAut G A gamma).hom =
84	      Spec.map
85	        (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A gamma⁻¹)) :=
86	  rfl
87	
88	lemma toSpecAut_mul_hom (gamma tau : G) :
89	    (toSpecAut G A (gamma * tau)).hom =
90	      (toSpecAut G A tau).hom ≫ (toSpecAut G A gamma).hom := by
91	  rw [map_mul]
92	  rfl
93	
94	lemma toSpecAut_inv_hom (gamma : G) :
95	    (toSpecAut G A gamma⁻¹).hom = (toSpecAut G A gamma).inv := by
96	  rw [map_inv]
97	  rfl
98	
99	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
100	lemma toSpecAut_hom_inv_hom (gamma : G) :
101	    (toSpecAut G A gamma).hom ≫ (toSpecAut G A gamma⁻¹).hom = 𝟙 _ := by
102	  rw [toSpecAut_inv_hom, Iso.hom_inv_id]
103	
104	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
105	lemma toSpecAut_inv_hom_hom (gamma : G) :
106	    (toSpecAut G A gamma⁻¹).hom ≫ (toSpecAut G A gamma).hom = 𝟙 _ := by
107	  rw [toSpecAut_inv_hom, Iso.inv_hom_id]
108	
109	end SpecAut
110	
111	variable (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
112	
113	/-- A semilinear action of the `K`-algebra automorphisms of `L` on an
114	`L`-scheme.  Each automorphism of the total space covers the corresponding
115	automorphism of `Spec L`. -/
116	structure SemilinearGalAction (X : Scheme.{u})
117	    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) where
118	  act : (L ≃ₐ[K] L) →* Aut X
119	  compat (gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
120	    (act gamma).hom ≫ f =
121	      f ≫ (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) L gamma).hom
122	
123	namespace SemilinearGalAction
124	
125	variable {K L} {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
126	
127	/-- Equivariance of a morphism between semilinearly acted schemes. -/
128	def IsEquivariant {X' : Scheme.{u}}
129	    {f' : X' ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
130	    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
131	    (rho' : SemilinearGalAction K L X' f') (h : X ⟶ X') : Prop :=
132	  ∀ gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L,
133	    (rho.act gamma).hom ≫ h = h ≫ (rho'.act gamma).hom

140	a scheme: every orbit lies in one affine open. -/
141	class OrbitsInAffineOpen (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) : Prop where
142	  exists_affineOpen (x : X) :
143	    ∃ U : X.affineOpens,
144	      ∀ gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L, (rho.act gamma).hom.base x ∈ U.1

147	def IsStableOpen (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (U : X.Opens) : Prop :=

155	    {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
156	    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) : Prop where
157	  exists_stable_affineOpen (x : X) :
158	    ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧ rho.IsStableOpen U

14	/-!
15	# Galois descent for semilinear representations (Speiser's theorem)
16	
17	This file supplies the **finite Galois descent** substrate for the FGA Picard-scheme
18	representability campaign (`instHasPicScheme`, cluster `G` of
19	`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`): milestone `G2(b)` (Speiser's
20	semilinear descent) and its consumers `G1`/`G3`.
21	
22	Let `L/K` be a finite Galois extension with group `G = Gal(L/K) = L ≃ₐ[K] L`, and
23	let `V` be an `L`-vector space equipped with a **semilinear** `G`-action, i.e. an
24	additive `G`-action with
25	`σ • (a • v) = σ a • (σ • v)` for `σ ∈ G`, `a ∈ L`, `v ∈ V` (`IsSemilinear`).
26	The `K`-subspace of invariants `V^G` (`SemilinearAction.invariants`) is a `K`-form
27	of `V`: the canonical `L`-linear map
28	
29	`descentMap : L ⊗[K] V^G → V`,  `a ⊗ v ↦ a • v`
30	
31	is an **isomorphism** (`descentEquiv`), so `dim_K V^G = dim_L V`. This is Speiser's
32	theorem — Galois descent for vector spaces — the algebraic heart of the finite
33	Galois quotient engine `G2`.
34	
35	## Main definitions and results
36	
37	* `IsSemilinear K L V` — the semilinearity hypothesis on a `G`-action.
38	* `SemilinearAction.invariants K L V : Submodule K V` — the fixed subspace `V^G`.
39	* `SemilinearAction.avg K L a v : V` — the averaging element `∑_σ σ a • (σ • v)`,
40	  which always lies in `V^G` (`avg_mem_invariants`).
41	* `SemilinearAction.descentMap K L V : L ⊗[K] V^G →ₗ[L] V` — the descent map.
42	* `SemilinearAction.descentMap_bijective` / `descentEquiv` — Speiser's theorem.
43	
44	## Mathlib inputs
45	
46	The linear-algebra heart is **Dedekind's independence of characters**
47	(`linearIndependent_algHom_toLinearMap`): the `K`-algebra homomorphisms `L →ₐ[K] L`
48	are `L`-linearly independent as `K`-linear maps.  Combined with the finite-field
49	count `AlgHom.card`, the "Galois matrix" `(σ (b i))_{σ, i}` of a `K`-basis `b` of
50	`L` is invertible over `L`, which powers both directions of the descent isomorphism.
51	
52	Campaign reference: milestone `G2` of `informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`
53	(Kleiman §4 uses finite Galois descent to build `Pic_{C/k}` from `Pic_{C_{k'}/k'}`;
54	this brick is field-agnostic and reused for `Sym^d`/Albanese).
55	-/

63	
64	variable (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
65	variable (V : Type v) [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [Module L V] [IsScalarTower K L V]
66	variable [DistribMulAction (L ≃ₐ[K] L) V]

68	/-- A **semilinear** `Gal(L/K)`-action on an `L`-module `V`: the additive `G`-action
69	is compatible with the `L`-scalar action twisted by `σ`, i.e.
70	`σ • (a • v) = σ a • (σ • v)`. -/
71	class IsSemilinear : Prop where
72	  /-- The semilinearity relation `σ • (a • v) = σ a • (σ • v)`. -/
73	  smul_smul' (σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) (a : L) (v : V) : σ • (a • v) = σ a • σ • v
74	
75	/-! ## The Galois matrix
76	
77	Dedekind's independence of characters, transported through evaluation at a
78	`K`-basis `b` of `L`, says the "rows" of the Galois matrix `(σ (b i))_{σ, i}` are
79	`L`-linearly independent in `ι → L`; since their number equals `dim_L (ι → L)`
80	they span.  From this we deduce the annihilation criterion
81	`galoisMatrix_eq_zero_of`, which powers both directions of Speiser descent. -/
82	
83	section GaloisCore
84	
85	variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
86	variable {ι : Type*}
87	
88	/-- Evaluation of a `K`-linear endomorphism of `L` at a basis, as an `L`-linear map
89	`(L →ₗ[K] L) →ₗ[L] (ι → L)`, `f ↦ (i ↦ f (b i))`. -/
90	noncomputable def evalAtBasis (b : Basis ι K L) : (L →ₗ[K] L) →ₗ[L] (ι → L) where
91	  toFun f i := f (b i)
92	  map_add' f g := by ext i; simp
93	  map_smul' c f := by ext i; simp
94	
95	omit [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] in
96	@[simp] lemma evalAtBasis_apply (b : Basis ι K L) (f : L →ₗ[K] L) (i : ι) :
97	    evalAtBasis b f i = f (b i) := rfl
98	
99	omit [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] in
100	lemma evalAtBasis_ker (b : Basis ι K L) : LinearMap.ker (evalAtBasis b) = ⊥ := by
101	  rw [LinearMap.ker_eq_bot']
102	  intro f hf
103	  refine b.ext fun i => ?_
104	  have h0 : evalAtBasis b f i = 0 := by rw [hf]; rfl
105	  simpa using h0

107	omit [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] in
108	/-- **Dedekind independence, matrix form.** The rows `σ ↦ (i ↦ σ (b i))` of the
109	Galois matrix are `L`-linearly independent in `ι → L`. -/
110	theorem galoisRow_linearIndependent (b : Basis ι K L) :
111	    LinearIndependent L (fun σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L => (fun i => σ (b i) : ι → L)) := by
112	  have hAlg : LinearIndependent L (fun f : L →ₐ[K] L => f.toLinearMap) :=
113	    linearIndependent_algHom_toLinearMap K L L
114	  have hEquiv : LinearIndependent L
115	      (fun σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L => ((σ : L →ₐ[K] L)).toLinearMap) :=
116	    hAlg.comp (fun σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L => (σ : L →ₐ[K] L)) AlgEquiv.coe_algHom_injective
117	  have hmap := hEquiv.map' (evalAtBasis b) (evalAtBasis_ker b)
118	  have hfun : (fun σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L => (fun i => σ (b i) : ι → L))
119	      = (evalAtBasis b) ∘ (fun σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L => ((σ : L →ₐ[K] L)).toLinearMap) := by
120	    funext σ i; simp
121	  rw [hfun]; exact hmap
122	
123	/-- The rows of the Galois matrix span `ι → L` over `L`. -/
124	theorem galoisRow_span [Finite ι] (b : Basis ι K L) :
125	    Submodule.span L (Set.range (fun σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L => (fun i => σ (b i) : ι → L))) = ⊤ := by
126	  haveI := Fintype.ofFinite ι
127	  haveI : Nonempty ι := b.index_nonempty
128	  refine (galoisRow_linearIndependent b).span_eq_top_of_card_eq_finrank ?_
129	  have h1 : Fintype.card (L ≃ₐ[K] L) = Fintype.card ι := by
130	    rw [← Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank K L, finrank_eq_card_basis b]
131	  rw [Module.finrank_fintype_fun_eq_card, h1]
132	
133	/-- **The Galois-matrix annihilation criterion.** For any `L`-module `W` and
134	vectors `t : ι → W`: if `∑_i σ (b i) • t i = 0` for every `σ ∈ Gal(L/K)`, then all
135	`t i = 0`.  With `W = V` this gives injectivity of the descent map; with `W = L`
136	it gives independence of the Galois-matrix columns (hence surjectivity). -/
137	theorem galoisMatrix_eq_zero_of [Fintype ι]
138	    {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module L W]
139	    (b : Basis ι K L) (t : ι → W)
140	    (h : ∀ σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, ∑ i, σ (b i) • t i = 0) (j : ι) : t j = 0 := by
141	  classical
142	  have hmem : (Pi.single j (1 : L) : ι → L) ∈ Submodule.span L
143	      (Set.range (fun σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L => (fun i => σ (b i) : ι → L))) := by
144	    rw [galoisRow_span]; trivial
145	  rw [Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun] at hmem
146	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hmem
147	  have hcoord : ∀ i, (Pi.single j (1 : L) : ι → L) i = ∑ σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, c σ * σ (b i) := by
148	    intro i
149	    have := congrFun hc i
150	    simpa [Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul] using this.symm
151	  calc t j = ∑ i, (Pi.single j (1 : L) : ι → L) i • t i := by
152	            simp [Pi.single_apply, Finset.sum_ite_eq']
153	    _ = ∑ i, (∑ σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, c σ * σ (b i)) • t i := by
154	            refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_; rw [hcoord i]
155	    _ = ∑ σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, c σ • ∑ i, σ (b i) • t i := by
156	            simp_rw [Finset.sum_smul, mul_smul]
157	            rw [Finset.sum_comm]
158	            simp_rw [← Finset.smul_sum]
159	    _ = 0 := by simp [h]
160	
161	/-- The columns of the Galois matrix span `(L ≃ₐ[K] L) → L` over `L`.  Deduced from
162	column independence (`galoisMatrix_eq_zero_of` with `W = L`) and the cardinality
163	count.  Powers surjectivity of the descent map. -/
164	theorem galoisCol_span [Finite ι] (b : Basis ι K L) :
165	    Submodule.span L
166	      (Set.range (fun i : ι => (fun σ => σ (b i) : (L ≃ₐ[K] L) → L))) = ⊤ := by
167	  classical
168	  haveI := Fintype.ofFinite ι
169	  haveI : Nonempty ι := b.index_nonempty
170	  have hindep : LinearIndependent L
171	      (fun i : ι => (fun σ => σ (b i) : (L ≃ₐ[K] L) → L)) := by
172	    rw [Fintype.linearIndependent_iff]
173	    intro g hg
174	    refine galoisMatrix_eq_zero_of b g fun σ => ?_
175	    have h2 := congrFun hg σ
176	    simp only [Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, Pi.zero_apply] at h2
177	    simpa [smul_eq_mul, mul_comm] using h2
178	  refine hindep.span_eq_top_of_card_eq_finrank ?_
179	  have h1 : Fintype.card ι = Fintype.card (L ≃ₐ[K] L) := by
180	    rw [← Nat.card_eq_fintype_card (α := L ≃ₐ[K] L), IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank K L,
181	      finrank_eq_card_basis b]
182	  rw [Module.finrank_fintype_fun_eq_card, h1]
183	
184	/-- From an `L`-basis `b` of `L` and a `K`-module `W`: the `K`-linear map
185	`(ι → W) → L ⊗[K] W`, `t ↦ ∑ i, b i ⊗ₜ t i`.  It is surjective, exhibiting
186	`L ⊗[K] W` as spanned by the tensors `b i ⊗ₜ w`. -/
187	noncomputable def tensorFromPi [Fintype ι] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W]
188	    (b : Basis ι K L) : (ι → W) →ₗ[K] L ⊗[K] W :=
189	  ∑ i, (TensorProduct.mk K L W (b i)).comp (LinearMap.proj i)
190	
191	omit [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] in
192	lemma tensorFromPi_apply [Fintype ι] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W]
193	    (b : Basis ι K L) (t : ι → W) :
194	    tensorFromPi b t = ∑ i, b i ⊗ₜ[K] t i := by
195	  simp [tensorFromPi, LinearMap.sum_apply]

197	omit [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] in
198	lemma tensorFromPi_surjective [Fintype ι] {W : Type*} [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W]
199	    (b : Basis ι K L) : Function.Surjective (tensorFromPi (W := W) b) := by
200	  intro x
201	  induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on with
202	  | zero => exact ⟨0, by simp [tensorFromPi_apply]⟩
203	  | tmul a w =>
204	      refine ⟨fun i => b.repr a i • w, ?_⟩
205	      rw [tensorFromPi_apply]
206	      conv_rhs => rw [← Basis.sum_repr b a]
207	      rw [TensorProduct.sum_tmul]
208	      exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => (TensorProduct.smul_tmul _ _ _).symm
209	  | add x y hx hy =>
210	      obtain ⟨tx, rfl⟩ := hx
211	      obtain ⟨ty, rfl⟩ := hy
212	      exact ⟨tx + ty, by rw [map_add]⟩

214	end GaloisCore

221	lemma smul_smul_apply [IsSemilinear K L V]
222	    (σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) (a : L) (v : V) : σ • (a • v) = σ a • σ • v :=
223	  IsSemilinear.smul_smul' σ a v

225	variable (K L V)
226	
227	/-- The `K`-subspace `V^G` of `Gal(L/K)`-invariant vectors. It is a `K`-submodule
228	(not `L`) because the `G`-action is only `K`-semilinear. -/
229	def invariants [IsSemilinear K L V] : Submodule K V where
230	  carrier := {v | ∀ σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, σ • v = v}
231	  add_mem' {x y} hx hy σ := by rw [smul_add, hx, hy]
232	  zero_mem' σ := smul_zero σ
233	  smul_mem' c v hv σ := by
234	    -- `c : K` acts through `L`; `σ` fixes `K`, so it fixes `c • v`.
235	    rw [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_smul L c v, smul_smul_apply, AlgEquiv.commutes, hv]
236	
237	@[simp] lemma mem_invariants [IsSemilinear K L V] {v : V} :
238	    v ∈ invariants K L V ↔ ∀ σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, σ • v = v := Iff.rfl

242	/-- The **averaging** element `∑_σ σ a • (σ • v)`.  For every `a : L` and `v : V`
243	it lies in the invariants `V^G` (`avg_mem_invariants`); ranging `a` over `L` it
244	produces enough invariants to span `V` over `L` (`span_avg_eq_top`). -/
245	noncomputable def avg [FiniteDimensional K L] (a : L) (v : V) : V :=
246	  ∑ σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, σ a • σ • v

250	lemma avg_mem_invariants [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsSemilinear K L V] (a : L) (v : V) :
251	    avg K L a v ∈ invariants K L V := by
252	  intro τ
253	  have hτ : τ • avg K L a v = ∑ σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, (τ * σ) a • (τ * σ) • v := by
254	    rw [avg, Finset.smul_sum]
255	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun σ _ => ?_
256	    rw [smul_smul_apply, ← mul_smul, ← AlgEquiv.mul_apply]
257	  rw [hτ, avg]
258	  exact Equiv.sum_comp (Equiv.mulLeft τ) (fun σ => σ a • σ • v)
259	
260	variable (K L V)
261	
262	/-- The **descent map** `L ⊗[K] V^G →ₗ[L] V`, `a ⊗ v ↦ a • v`, the `L`-linear
263	extension of the `K`-linear inclusion `V^G ↪ V`.  Speiser's theorem
264	(`descentMap_bijective`) is that it is bijective. -/
265	noncomputable def descentMap [IsSemilinear K L V] :
266	    L ⊗[K] (invariants K L V) →ₗ[L] V :=
267	  TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.lift
268	    (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton L _ (invariants K L V).subtype)
269	
270	@[simp] lemma descentMap_tmul [IsSemilinear K L V] (a : L) (w : invariants K L V) :
271	    descentMap K L V (a ⊗ₜ[K] w) = a • (w : V) := by
272	  simp [descentMap, LinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply, LinearMap.smul_apply]
273	
274	/-! ## Speiser's theorem: the descent map is an isomorphism -/
275	
276	variable [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
277	
278	/-- **Surjectivity direction.** The invariants `V^G` span `V` over `L`.  For each
279	`v` and each basis vector `b i`, the averaged element `avg (b i) v` is invariant,
280	and `v` is recovered as an `L`-combination of these because the columns of the
281	Galois matrix span (`galoisCol_span`). -/
282	theorem span_invariants_eq_top [IsSemilinear K L V] :
283	    Submodule.span L ((invariants K L V : Set V)) = ⊤ := by
284	  classical
285	  rw [Submodule.eq_top_iff']
286	  intro v
287	  set b := finBasis K L with hb
288	  set Ψ : ((L ≃ₐ[K] L) → L) →ₗ[L] V :=
289	    Fintype.linearCombination L (fun σ => σ • v) with hΨ
290	  have hv : Ψ (Pi.single (1 : L ≃ₐ[K] L) (1 : L)) = v := by
291	    simp [hΨ, Fintype.linearCombination_apply_single, one_smul]
292	  have hcol : (Pi.single (1 : L ≃ₐ[K] L) (1 : L)) ∈ Submodule.span L
293	      (Set.range (fun i => (fun σ => σ (b i) : (L ≃ₐ[K] L) → L))) := by
294	    rw [galoisCol_span b]; trivial
295	  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun L).mp hcol
296	  have hΨcol : ∀ i, Ψ (fun σ => σ (b i)) = avg K L (b i) v := fun i => by
297	    rw [hΨ, Fintype.linearCombination_apply]; rfl
298	  have hveq : ∑ i, e i • avg K L (b i) v = v := by
299	    calc ∑ i, e i • avg K L (b i) v
300	        = ∑ i, e i • Ψ (fun σ => σ (b i)) := by
301	            refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_; rw [hΨcol i]
302	      _ = Ψ (∑ i, e i • fun σ => σ (b i)) := by rw [map_sum]; simp_rw [map_smul]
303	      _ = Ψ (Pi.single 1 1) := by rw [he]
304	      _ = v := hv
305	  rw [← hveq]
306	  exact Submodule.sum_mem _ fun i _ => Submodule.smul_mem _ _
307	    (Submodule.subset_span (avg_mem_invariants (b i) v))
308	
309	/-- **Surjectivity of the descent map** `L ⊗[K] V^G → V`. -/
310	theorem descentMap_surjective [IsSemilinear K L V] :
311	    Function.Surjective (descentMap K L V) := by
312	  rw [← LinearMap.range_eq_top]
313	  refine top_le_iff.mp ?_
314	  rw [← span_invariants_eq_top K L V]
315	  refine Submodule.span_le.mpr ?_
316	  intro x hx
317	  exact ⟨1 ⊗ₜ[K] (⟨x, hx⟩ : invariants K L V), by simp⟩
318	
319	/-- **Injectivity of the descent map** `L ⊗[K] V^G → V`.  Writing an element via the
320	basis `b` of `L` as `∑ i, b i ⊗ t i` (`tensorFromPi_surjective`), the image
321	`∑ i, b i • t i = 0` and the invariance of the `t i` feed the Galois-matrix
322	annihilation criterion `galoisMatrix_eq_zero_of`, forcing every `t i = 0`. -/
323	theorem descentMap_injective [IsSemilinear K L V] :
324	    Function.Injective (descentMap K L V) := by
325	  classical
326	  set b := finBasis K L with hb
327	  -- The composite `t ↦ descentMap (∑ i, b i ⊗ t i) = ∑ i, b i • t i` is injective.
328	  have hcompose : ∀ t : Fin (finrank K L) → invariants K L V,
329	      descentMap K L V (tensorFromPi b t) = ∑ i, b i • ((t i : V)) := by
330	    intro t
331	    rw [tensorFromPi_apply, map_sum]
332	    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => descentMap_tmul K L V (b i) (t i)
333	  have hcomp_inj : Function.Injective
334	      (fun t : Fin (finrank K L) → invariants K L V => descentMap K L V (tensorFromPi b t)) := by
335	    intro t s hts
336	    replace hts : ∑ i, b i • ((t i : V)) = ∑ i, b i • ((s i : V)) := by
337	      rw [← hcompose, ← hcompose]; exact hts
338	    funext j
339	    have hu : ∀ σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, ∑ i, σ (b i) • ((t i : V) - (s i : V)) = 0 := by
340	      intro σ
341	      have hdiff : ∑ i, b i • ((t i : V) - (s i : V)) = 0 := by
342	        simp_rw [smul_sub, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, hts, sub_self]
343	      have key : σ • (∑ i, b i • ((t i : V) - (s i : V)))
344	          = ∑ i, σ (b i) • ((t i : V) - (s i : V)) := by
345	        rw [Finset.smul_sum]
346	        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
347	        rw [smul_smul_apply]
348	        congr 1
349	        rw [smul_sub, (t i).property σ, (s i).property σ]
350	      rw [← key, hdiff, smul_zero]
351	    have hzero := galoisMatrix_eq_zero_of b (fun i => (t i : V) - (s i : V)) hu j
352	    exact Subtype.ext (sub_eq_zero.mp hzero)
353	  intro x y hxy
354	  obtain ⟨t, rfl⟩ := tensorFromPi_surjective b x
355	  obtain ⟨s, rfl⟩ := tensorFromPi_surjective b y
356	  exact congrArg (tensorFromPi b) (hcomp_inj hxy)
357	
358	/-- **Speiser's theorem, bijectivity.** The descent map `L ⊗[K] V^G → V` is
359	bijective. -/
360	theorem descentMap_bijective [IsSemilinear K L V] :
361	    Function.Bijective (descentMap K L V) :=
362	  ⟨descentMap_injective K L V, descentMap_surjective K L V⟩
363	
364	/-- **Speiser's theorem.** For a finite Galois extension `L/K` and an `L`-vector
365	space `V` with a semilinear `Gal(L/K)`-action, the descent map is an `L`-linear
366	isomorphism `L ⊗[K] V^G ≃ₗ[L] V`.  Thus `V^G` is a `K`-form of `V`. -/
367	noncomputable def descentEquiv [IsSemilinear K L V] :
368	    L ⊗[K] (invariants K L V) ≃ₗ[L] V :=
369	  LinearEquiv.ofBijective (descentMap K L V) (descentMap_bijective K L V)
370	
371	@[simp] lemma descentEquiv_tmul [IsSemilinear K L V] (a : L) (w : invariants K L V) :
372	    descentEquiv K L V (a ⊗ₜ[K] w) = a • (w : V) :=
373	  descentMap_tmul K L V a w
374	
375	/-- **Corollary (Galois descent of dimension).** `dim_K V^G = dim_L V`: the
376	invariants `V^G` form a `K`-form of the semilinear representation `V`. -/
377	theorem finrank_invariants [IsSemilinear K L V] :
378	    Module.finrank K (invariants K L V) = Module.finrank L V := by
379	  have h := (descentEquiv K L V).finrank_eq
380	  rwa [Module.finrank_baseChange] at h
381	
382	end SemilinearAction
383	
384	/-! ## The regular representation
385	
386	The natural `Gal(L/K)`-action on `L` itself is semilinear, and its invariants are
387	`K` (Artin), so `descentEquiv` specialises to the base-change isomorphism
388	`L ⊗[K] L^{Gal} ≃ L`.  This confirms the framework on the universal example. -/
389	
390	/-- The natural `Gal(L/K)`-action on `L` (apply the automorphism) is semilinear for
391	the `L`-module structure of `L` on itself. -/
392	instance : IsSemilinear K L L where
393	  smul_smul' σ a b := by simp [smul_eq_mul, AlgEquiv.smul_def]
394	
395	end AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent

8	/-!
9	# Galois descent for semilinear algebras (the affine heart of `G2`)
10	
11	This file upgrades the module-level Speiser descent of
12	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.GaloisDescent.SemilinearModules` to **algebras**: it is the
13	affine heart `G2(b)` of the finite Galois quotient engine of the Picard
14	representability campaign (`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`, cluster `G`).
15	
16	Let `L/K` be a finite Galois extension with group `Γ = Gal(L/K) = L ≃ₐ[K] L`, and let
17	`A` be an `L`-algebra carrying a `Γ`-action by **ring** automorphisms
18	(`MulSemiringAction (L ≃ₐ[K] L) A`) that is **semilinear** over the Galois action on
19	`L` (`IsSemilinear K L A`, the landed module-level class; for a ring action it is
20	equivalent to `γ • algebraMap L A a = algebraMap L A (γ a)`, see `smul_algebraMap`
21	and `isSemilinear_of_smul_algebraMap`).
22	
23	## Main definitions and results
24	
25	* `SemilinearAction.invariantsSubalgebra K L A : Subalgebra K A` — the invariants
26	  `A^Γ` as a `K`-subalgebra (its underlying `K`-submodule is
27	  `SemilinearAction.invariants K L A`, definitionally).
28	* `SemilinearAction.descentAlgEquiv : L ⊗[K] A^Γ ≃ₐ[L] A` — **Speiser's theorem,
29	  algebra form**: the invariants are a `K`-form of `A` *as an algebra*.  Deduced from
30	  the module-level `descentEquiv`; in particular it does **not** use Noether-style
31	  invariant finiteness (the campaign's explicit prohibition), and `A` is arbitrary
32	  (no finiteness hypotheses).
33	* `Algebra.TensorProduct.mem_range_includeRight_iff_forall_map_eq` — for the
34	  left-factor Galois action on a base change `L ⊗[K] B` of any `K`-algebra `B`, the
35	  fixed points are exactly `1 ⊗ B`.
36	* `SemilinearAction.invariantAlgHomEquiv` — **the affine Hom property**:
37	  `Hom_{K-alg}(A^Γ, B) ≃ Hom_{L-alg}(A, L ⊗[K] B)^Γ` for every `K`-algebra `B`.
38	  Taking `B = Γ(T, 𝒪_T)` for an affine `K`-scheme `T = Spec B` this is precisely
39	  `Hom_K(T, Spec A^Γ) ≅ Hom_L(T_L, Spec A)^Γ`, the `T`-points statement of the
40	  Galois quotient `Spec A^Γ = (Spec A)/Γ` (scheme-level translation in
41	  `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FiniteGaloisQuotient`).
42	
43	The equivariance condition on `f : A →ₐ[L] L ⊗[K] B` is pinned inverse-free as
44	`IsEquivariantAlgHom`: `f (γ • x) = (γ ⊗ id) (f x)` for all `γ, x`.
45	
46	Campaign reference: milestone `G2(b)` of `informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`
47	(Kleiman FGA-explained §4, Milne JV §4 use finite Galois descent to build `Pic_{C/k}`
48	from `Pic_{C_{k'}/k'}`; this brick is curve-agnostic and reusable for
49	`Sym^d`/Albanese).
50	-/
51	
52	universe u v w

54	open scoped TensorProduct
55	open Module

57	namespace AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent
58	
59	variable (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
60	variable (A : Type v) [CommRing A] [Algebra K A] [Algebra L A] [IsScalarTower K L A]
61	variable [MulSemiringAction (L ≃ₐ[K] L) A]
62	
63	namespace SemilinearAction
64	
65	/-! ## Ring-level semilinearity -/
66	
67	section RingSemilinear
68	
69	omit [Algebra K A] [IsScalarTower K L A] in
70	/-- For a `Γ`-action by ring automorphisms, semilinearity over the Galois action on
71	`L` specialises on the image of `L` to `γ • algebraMap L A a = algebraMap L A (γ a)`. -/
72	theorem smul_algebraMap [IsSemilinear K L A] (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) (a : L) :
73	    γ • (algebraMap L A a) = algebraMap L A (γ a) := by
74	  rw [Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one, Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one,
75	    smul_smul_apply, smul_one]
76	
77	omit [Algebra K A] [IsScalarTower K L A] in
78	/-- Conversely, a ring action satisfying `γ • algebraMap L A a = algebraMap L A (γ a)`
79	is semilinear.  This is the practical constructor for `IsSemilinear` on algebras. -/
80	theorem isSemilinear_of_smul_algebraMap
81	    (h : ∀ (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) (a : L), γ • (algebraMap L A a) = algebraMap L A (γ a)) :
82	    IsSemilinear K L A where
83	  smul_smul' γ a v := by
84	    rw [Algebra.smul_def, smul_mul', h, ← Algebra.smul_def]
85	
86	/-- The Galois action on `A` commutes with the `K`-scalar action (the Galois group
87	fixes `K`).  Enables mathlib's `FixedPoints.subalgebra`-style API. -/
88	instance [IsSemilinear K L A] : SMulCommClass (L ≃ₐ[K] L) K A where
89	  smul_comm γ c x := by
90	    rw [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_smul L c x, smul_smul_apply, AlgEquiv.commutes,
91	      IsScalarTower.algebraMap_smul]
92	
93	end RingSemilinear
94	
95	/-! ## The invariant subalgebra -/
96	
97	section InvariantsSubalgebra
98	
99	variable [IsSemilinear K L A]
100	
101	/-- The invariants `A^Γ` of a semilinear `Gal(L/K)`-action by ring automorphisms, as
102	a `K`-subalgebra of `A`.  Its underlying `K`-submodule is
103	`SemilinearAction.invariants K L A` (`toSubmodule_invariantsSubalgebra`). -/
104	def invariantsSubalgebra : Subalgebra K A where
105	  carrier := {a | ∀ σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, σ • a = a}
106	  mul_mem' {x y} hx hy σ := by rw [smul_mul', hx σ, hy σ]
107	  one_mem' σ := smul_one σ
108	  add_mem' {x y} hx hy σ := by rw [smul_add, hx σ, hy σ]
109	  zero_mem' σ := smul_zero σ
110	  algebraMap_mem' r σ := by
111	    rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply K L A, smul_algebraMap K L A, AlgEquiv.commutes]
112	
113	@[simp] lemma mem_invariantsSubalgebra {a : A} :
114	    a ∈ invariantsSubalgebra K L A ↔ ∀ σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, σ • a = a := Iff.rfl
115	
116	@[simp] lemma toSubmodule_invariantsSubalgebra :
117	    Subalgebra.toSubmodule (invariantsSubalgebra K L A) = invariants K L A := rfl
118	
119	/-- The tautological `K`-linear equivalence between the subalgebra invariants and the
120	module-level invariants (same carrier). -/
121	def invariantsLinearEquiv :
122	    (invariantsSubalgebra K L A) ≃ₗ[K] (invariants K L A) where
123	  toFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
124	  map_add' _ _ := rfl
125	  map_smul' _ _ := rfl
126	  invFun x := ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
127	  left_inv _ := rfl
128	  right_inv _ := rfl
129	
130	@[simp] lemma invariantsLinearEquiv_coe (x : invariantsSubalgebra K L A) :
131	    ((invariantsLinearEquiv K L A x : invariants K L A) : A) = (x : A) := rfl
132	
133	end InvariantsSubalgebra
134	
135	/-! ## Speiser's theorem, algebra form -/
136	
137	section DescentAlgEquiv
138	
139	variable [IsSemilinear K L A]
140	
141	/-- The descent map `L ⊗[K] A^Γ →ₐ[L] A`, `a ⊗ w ↦ a • w`, as an `L`-algebra
142	homomorphism (the `L`-linear extension of the inclusion `A^Γ ↪ A`).  Its underlying
143	map agrees with the module-level `SemilinearAction.descentMap`. -/
144	noncomputable def descentAlgHom : L ⊗[K] (invariantsSubalgebra K L A) →ₐ[L] A :=
145	  AlgHom.liftEquiv K L _ A (invariantsSubalgebra K L A).val
146	
147	@[simp] lemma descentAlgHom_tmul (a : L) (w : invariantsSubalgebra K L A) :
148	    descentAlgHom K L A (a ⊗ₜ[K] w) = a • (w : A) := rfl
149	
150	variable [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
151	
152	/-- **Speiser's theorem, algebra form (bijectivity).**  Deduced from the module-level
153	`descentMap_bijective` — never via invariant finiteness. -/
154	theorem descentAlgHom_bijective : Function.Bijective (descentAlgHom K L A) := by
155	  have heq : ⇑(descentAlgHom K L A) = ⇑(descentMap K L A) ∘
156	      ⇑(TensorProduct.congr (LinearEquiv.refl K L) (invariantsLinearEquiv K L A)) := by
157	    funext y
158	    induction y using TensorProduct.induction_on with
159	    | zero => simp
160	    | tmul a w =>
161	        simp only [Function.comp_apply, descentAlgHom_tmul, TensorProduct.congr_tmul,
162	          LinearEquiv.refl_apply, descentMap_tmul, invariantsLinearEquiv_coe]
163	    | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy, Function.comp_apply]
164	  rw [heq]
165	  exact (descentMap_bijective K L A).comp (TensorProduct.congr _ _).bijective
166	
167	/-- **Speiser's theorem, algebra form.**  For a finite Galois extension `L/K` and an
168	`L`-algebra `A` with a semilinear `Gal(L/K)`-action by ring automorphisms, the descent
169	map is an `L`-algebra isomorphism `L ⊗[K] A^Γ ≃ₐ[L] A`: the invariant subalgebra is a
170	`K`-form of `A`. -/
171	noncomputable def descentAlgEquiv : L ⊗[K] (invariantsSubalgebra K L A) ≃ₐ[L] A :=
172	  AlgEquiv.ofBijective (descentAlgHom K L A) (descentAlgHom_bijective K L A)
173	
174	@[simp] lemma descentAlgEquiv_tmul (a : L) (w : invariantsSubalgebra K L A) :
175	    descentAlgEquiv K L A (a ⊗ₜ[K] w) = a • (w : A) := rfl
176	
177	lemma descentAlgEquiv_symm_coe (w : invariantsSubalgebra K L A) :
178	    (descentAlgEquiv K L A).symm (w : A) = 1 ⊗ₜ[K] w := by
179	  rw [AlgEquiv.symm_apply_eq, descentAlgEquiv_tmul, one_smul]
180	
181	/-- Galois equivariance of the descent isomorphism: the left-factor action `γ ⊗ id`
182	on `L ⊗[K] A^Γ` corresponds to the given action on `A`. -/
183	theorem descentAlgEquiv_map_left (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L)
184	    (y : L ⊗[K] (invariantsSubalgebra K L A)) :
185	    descentAlgEquiv K L A
186	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (γ : L →ₐ[K] L) (AlgHom.id K _) y)
187	      = γ • descentAlgEquiv K L A y := by
188	  induction y using TensorProduct.induction_on with
189	  | zero => simp
190	  | tmul a w =>
191	      rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul, AlgHom.coe_id, id_eq, AlgEquiv.coe_algHom,
192	        descentAlgEquiv_tmul, descentAlgEquiv_tmul, smul_smul_apply, w.2 γ]
193	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, smul_add, hx, hy]
194	
195	end DescentAlgEquiv
196	
197	end SemilinearAction
198	
199	/-! ## Fixed points of the left-factor Galois action on a base change
200	
201	For any `K`-algebra `B`, the Galois group acts on `L ⊗[K] B` through the left factor
202	(`γ ⊗ id`); the fixed points are exactly the image of `includeRight : B → L ⊗[K] B`.
203	This is the "trivially-descended" case of Speiser, proved directly by a
204	basis-coordinate computation (any `K`-basis of `B` base-changes to an `L`-basis whose
205	coordinates transform by `γ`). -/
206	
207	section BaseChangeFixedPoints
208	
209	variable [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
210	variable (B : Type w) [CommRing B] [Algebra K B]
211	
212	omit [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] in
213	open Algebra.TensorProduct in
214	/-- Coordinates of the left-factor Galois action: in the base-changed basis
215	`1 ⊗ bᵢ` of `L ⊗[K] B`, the action `γ ⊗ id` acts on coordinates by `γ`. -/
216	lemma repr_map_left_baseChange {ι : Type*} (b : Basis ι K B) (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L)
217	    (x : L ⊗[K] B) (i : ι) :
218	    (b.baseChange L).repr (map (γ : L →ₐ[K] L) (AlgHom.id K B) x) i
219	      = γ ((b.baseChange L).repr x i) := by
220	  induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on with
221	  | zero => simp
222	  | tmul l y =>
223	      rw [map_tmul, AlgHom.coe_id, id_eq, AlgEquiv.coe_algHom,
224	        Basis.baseChange_repr_tmul, Basis.baseChange_repr_tmul, map_smul]
225	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, Finsupp.add_apply, hx, hy]
226	
227	open Algebra.TensorProduct in
228	/-- **Fixed points of the base change.**  For the left-factor Galois action on
229	`L ⊗[K] B`, an element is fixed by all `γ ⊗ id` iff it lies in `1 ⊗ B`. -/
230	theorem mem_range_includeRight_iff_forall_map_eq (x : L ⊗[K] B) :
231	    x ∈ (includeRight : B →ₐ[K] L ⊗[K] B).range
232	      ↔ ∀ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, map (γ : L →ₐ[K] L) (AlgHom.id K B) x = x := by
233	  constructor
234	  · rintro ⟨y, rfl⟩ γ
235	    simp only [AlgHom.toRingHom_eq_coe, AlgHom.coe_toRingHom]
236	    rw [includeRight_apply, map_tmul, map_one, AlgHom.coe_id, id_eq]
237	  · intro hx
238	    classical
239	    let b := Module.Free.chooseBasis K B
240	    set bb := b.baseChange L with hbb
241	    have hfix : ∀ i, ∀ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, γ (bb.repr x i) = bb.repr x i := by
242	      intro i γ
243	      conv_rhs => rw [← hx γ]
244	      rw [repr_map_left_baseChange K L B b γ x i]
245	    have hmem : ∀ i, ∃ c : K, algebraMap K L c = bb.repr x i := fun i =>
246	      (IsGalois.mem_range_algebraMap_iff_fixed (bb.repr x i)).mpr (hfix i)
247	    choose c hc using hmem
248	    refine ⟨(bb.repr x).sum fun i _ => c i • b i, ?_⟩
249	    simp only [AlgHom.toRingHom_eq_coe, AlgHom.coe_toRingHom]
250	    rw [includeRight_apply]
251	    conv_rhs => rw [← bb.linearCombination_repr x]
252	    rw [Finsupp.linearCombination_apply, Finsupp.sum, Finsupp.sum, TensorProduct.tmul_sum]
253	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
254	    rw [TensorProduct.tmul_smul, ← hc i, ← algebraMap_smul L (c i) ((1 : L) ⊗ₜ[K] b i),

261	/-! ## The affine Hom property
262	
263	`Hom_{K-alg}(A^Γ, B) ≃ Hom_{L-alg}(A, L ⊗[K] B)^Γ` for every `K`-algebra `B`.  With
264	`B = Γ(T, 𝒪_T)`, `T = Spec B`, this is the `T`-points property of the affine Galois
265	quotient `Spec (A^Γ)`. -/
266	
267	section HomProperty
268	
269	variable [IsSemilinear K L A]
270	variable (B : Type w) [CommRing B] [Algebra K B]
271	
272	/-- Equivariance for an `L`-algebra map `f : A → L ⊗[K] B` (with the left-factor
273	Galois action on the target): `f (γ • x) = (γ ⊗ id) (f x)`.  This is the invariance
274	of `f` under the natural `Γ`-action `f ↦ (γ ⊗ id) ∘ f ∘ γ⁻¹` on homs, pinned
275	inverse-free. -/
276	def IsEquivariantAlgHom (f : A →ₐ[L] L ⊗[K] B) : Prop :=
277	  ∀ (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) (x : A),
278	    f (γ • x) = Algebra.TensorProduct.map (γ : L →ₐ[K] L) (AlgHom.id K B) (f x)
279	
280	variable [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
281	
282	/-- Extension of scalars of a `K`-algebra map on the invariants, through the descent
283	isomorphism: `A ≃ L ⊗ A^Γ → L ⊗ B`. -/
284	noncomputable def extendScalarsAlgHom (g : invariantsSubalgebra K L A →ₐ[K] B) :
285	    A →ₐ[L] L ⊗[K] B :=
286	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id L L) g).comp
287	    (descentAlgEquiv K L A).symm.toAlgHom
288	
289	@[simp] lemma extendScalarsAlgHom_coe (g : invariantsSubalgebra K L A →ₐ[K] B)
290	    (w : invariantsSubalgebra K L A) :
291	    extendScalarsAlgHom K L A B g (w : A)
292	      = Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (g w) := by
293	  rw [extendScalarsAlgHom, AlgHom.comp_apply, AlgEquiv.coe_algHom,
294	    descentAlgEquiv_symm_coe, Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul, map_one,
295	    Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight_apply]
296	
297	omit [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] in
298	/-- Naturality: the left-factor action commutes with `id ⊗ g`. -/
299	lemma map_left_map_right_comm (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) (g : invariantsSubalgebra K L A →ₐ[K] B)
300	    (y : L ⊗[K] (invariantsSubalgebra K L A)) :
301	    Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id L L) g
302	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (γ : L →ₐ[K] L) (AlgHom.id K _) y)
303	      = Algebra.TensorProduct.map (γ : L →ₐ[K] L) (AlgHom.id K B)
304	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id L L) g y) := by
305	  induction y using TensorProduct.induction_on with
306	  | zero => simp
307	  | tmul a w => simp
308	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
309	
310	/-- The extension of scalars of an invariants-level map is equivariant. -/
311	theorem isEquivariantAlgHom_extendScalarsAlgHom (g : invariantsSubalgebra K L A →ₐ[K] B) :
312	    IsEquivariantAlgHom K L A B (extendScalarsAlgHom K L A B g) := by
313	  intro γ x
314	  have h1 : (descentAlgEquiv K L A).symm (γ • x)
315	      = Algebra.TensorProduct.map (γ : L →ₐ[K] L) (AlgHom.id K _)
316	          ((descentAlgEquiv K L A).symm x) := by
317	    apply (descentAlgEquiv K L A).injective
318	    rw [AlgEquiv.apply_symm_apply, descentAlgEquiv_map_left, AlgEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
319	  rw [extendScalarsAlgHom, AlgHom.comp_apply, AlgHom.comp_apply, AlgEquiv.coe_algHom,
320	    h1, map_left_map_right_comm]
321	
322	omit [FiniteDimensional K L] in
323	lemma includeRight_injective' :
324	    Function.Injective (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : B →ₐ[K] L ⊗[K] B) :=
325	  Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight_injective (FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective K L)
326	
327	/-- An equivariant `L`-algebra map sends invariants into `1 ⊗ B`. -/
328	lemma isEquivariantAlgHom_coe_mem_range {f : A →ₐ[L] L ⊗[K] B}
329	    (hf : IsEquivariantAlgHom K L A B f) (w : invariantsSubalgebra K L A) :
330	    f (w : A) ∈ (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : B →ₐ[K] L ⊗[K] B).range := by
331	  rw [mem_range_includeRight_iff_forall_map_eq]
332	  intro γ
333	  rw [← hf γ (w : A), w.2 γ]
334	
335	/-- Restriction of an equivariant `L`-algebra map `A → L ⊗[K] B` to the invariants,
336	landing in `B` (through `1 ⊗ B`). -/
337	noncomputable def restrictInvariantsAlgHom (f : A →ₐ[L] L ⊗[K] B)
338	    (hf : IsEquivariantAlgHom K L A B f) : invariantsSubalgebra K L A →ₐ[K] B :=
339	  ((AlgEquiv.ofInjective _ (includeRight_injective' K L B)).symm.toAlgHom).comp
340	    (((f.restrictScalars K).comp (invariantsSubalgebra K L A).val).codRestrict
341	      (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight :
342	        B →ₐ[K] L ⊗[K] B).range
343	      fun w => isEquivariantAlgHom_coe_mem_range K L A B hf w)
344	
345	@[simp] lemma includeRight_restrictInvariantsAlgHom (f : A →ₐ[L] L ⊗[K] B)
346	    (hf : IsEquivariantAlgHom K L A B f) (w : invariantsSubalgebra K L A) :
347	    Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (restrictInvariantsAlgHom K L A B f hf w)
348	      = f (w : A) := by
349	  have key : ∀ y : (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : B →ₐ[K] L ⊗[K] B).range,
350	      Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight
351	        ((AlgEquiv.ofInjective _ (includeRight_injective' K L B)).symm y) = (y : L ⊗[K] B) := by
352	    intro y
353	    conv_rhs => rw [← AlgEquiv.apply_symm_apply
354	      (AlgEquiv.ofInjective _ (includeRight_injective' K L B)) y]
355	    rw [AlgEquiv.ofInjective_apply]
356	  rw [restrictInvariantsAlgHom, AlgHom.comp_apply, AlgEquiv.coe_algHom, key]
357	  rfl
358	
359	/-- **The affine Hom property (Speiser descent for homs).**  For every `K`-algebra
360	`B`, `K`-algebra maps `A^Γ → B` correspond to equivariant `L`-algebra maps
361	`A → L ⊗[K] B`.  With `B = Γ(T, 𝒪_T)` for affine `T` this is
362	`Hom_K(T, Spec A^Γ) ≅ Hom_L(T ×_K Spec L, Spec A)^Γ`. -/
363	noncomputable def invariantAlgHomEquiv :
364	    (invariantsSubalgebra K L A →ₐ[K] B) ≃
365	      {f : A →ₐ[L] L ⊗[K] B // IsEquivariantAlgHom K L A B f} where
366	  toFun g := ⟨extendScalarsAlgHom K L A B g,
367	    isEquivariantAlgHom_extendScalarsAlgHom K L A B g⟩
368	  invFun f := restrictInvariantsAlgHom K L A B f.1 f.2
369	  left_inv g := by
370	    ext w
371	    apply includeRight_injective' K L B
372	    rw [includeRight_restrictInvariantsAlgHom, extendScalarsAlgHom_coe]
373	  right_inv f := by
374	    refine Subtype.ext ?_
375	    apply AlgHom.toLinearMap_injective
376	    apply LinearMap.ext_on (span_invariants_eq_top K L A)
377	    intro x hx
378	    have hx' : x ∈ invariantsSubalgebra K L A := hx
379	    change extendScalarsAlgHom K L A B (restrictInvariantsAlgHom K L A B f.1 f.2) x = f.1 x
380	    have hxw : x = ((⟨x, hx'⟩ : invariantsSubalgebra K L A) : A) := rfl
381	    rw [hxw, extendScalarsAlgHom_coe, includeRight_restrictInvariantsAlgHom]
382	
383	end HomProperty
384	
385	end SemilinearAction

11	/-!
12	# The finite Galois quotient engine (campaign milestone `G2`, scheme layer)
13	
14	Let `k'/k` be a finite Galois extension with group `Γ = Gal(k'/k)` and let `X'` be a
15	`k'`-scheme with a **semilinear** `Γ`-action.  This file supplies the scheme-level
16	vocabulary and statements for the quotient engine `G2` of the Picard representability
17	campaign (`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`, cluster `G`): the `k`-scheme
18	`X = X'/Γ` with `Γ`-equivariant `X ×_k k' ≅ X'` and
19	`Hom_k(T, X) ≅ Hom_{k'}(T_{k'}, X')^Γ`.
20	
21	## Semilinearity at scheme level (audit, campaign checklist item — conventions)
22	
23	A semilinear action is a group homomorphism `act : Γ →* Aut X'` together with
24	commuting squares over the Galois action on the base: `(act γ).hom ≫ f = f ≫ Spec γ`
25	(`SemilinearGalAction`).  Conventions are **validated constructively** by the affine
26	model `specSemilinearGalAction`: for `X' = Spec A` with a `MulSemiringAction Γ A`
27	that is `IsSemilinear K L A`, the assignment `γ ↦ Spec (γ⁻¹ • ·)` (`toSpecAut`) is a
28	group homomorphism into `Aut (Spec A)` — the inversion is forced jointly by the
29	contravariance of `Spec` and mathlib's `Aut` group law (`(x*y).hom = y.hom ≫ x.hom`)
30	— and satisfies the commuting squares.
31	
32	## Hironaka trap (campaign audit item 8, BLOCKING — verdict recorded here)
33	
34	The **orbit-in-affine hypothesis** (`SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen`: every
35	`Γ`-orbit lies in an affine open) is **essential and non-technical**.  For a free
36	action of `ℤ/2` on Hironaka's smooth proper non-projective threefold swapping two
37	rational curves that meet no common affine open, the quotient does **not** exist as
38	a scheme (only as an algebraic space); this is the same counterexample genus as the
39	permanently-instance-free `HasSmoothProperQuotient` (`FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).
40	Consequently the quotient existence is **never** stated for a bare `X'`: every
41	statement below carries the orbit hypothesis (or is a `Prop`-gate with **no
42	instances**).  For the campaign consumer `J'_r` the hypothesis is supplied by the
43	Γ-stable covering `V_Σ` with Grassmannian-immersion certificates (plan `J5`/`R6`).
44	
45	## Main definitions and results
46	
47	* `toSpecAut G A : G →* Aut (Spec A)` — a group acting on a ring by ring
48	  automorphisms acts on `Spec A` by scheme automorphisms.
49	* `SemilinearGalAction K L X f` — semilinear `Gal(L/K)`-action on a scheme over
50	  `Spec L`.
51	* `specSemilinearGalAction` — the affine model (conventions validator).
52	* `pullbackSemilinearGalAction` — the canonical action on a base change
53	  `T ×_{Spec K} Spec L` through the second factor (used to *state* equivariance of
54	  the descent isomorphism and the `T`-points property).
55	* `SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` — the orbit-in-affine hypothesis class.
56	* `IsGaloisQuotient ρ g` — the full quotient predicate: `Γ`-equivariant base-change
57	  isomorphism **and** the universal `T`-points property
58	  `Hom_k(T, X) ≅ Hom_{k'}(T_{k'}, X')^Γ` (unique descent of equivariant morphisms).
59	* `HasStableAffineCover` — Γ-stable affine refinement, the EGA II 4.5.4 pattern
60	  (`finite point set in an affine open of a separated/quasi-projective scheme
61	  refines to a Γ-stable affine open`). **This is no longer a gate: `G2(a)` was
62	  discharged** and `StableAffineCover.lean:279`
63	  (`hasStableAffineCover_of_orbitsInAffineOpen`) is a global `instance` deriving
64	  it from `[ρ.OrbitsInAffineOpen]` alone. Measured (`review-ajc`, 2026-07-29):
65	  `infer_instance` succeeds for an *abstract* `ρ` carrying only the orbit
66	  hypothesis, and fails without it — so the orbit hypothesis is exactly what it
67	  costs. The three sentences in this file and in `FiniteGaloisQuotientAffine.lean`
68	  that called it instance-free predate that discharge.
69	* `HasGaloisQuotient` — `Prop`-gate. It **was** genuinely instance-free; it is not
70	  any more, and the residue is now precisely the **non-affine** case.
71	  `hasGaloisQuotient_of_isAffine` (`Picard/GaloisQuotientAffineGeneral.lean`) is a
72	  global `instance` discharging it for `[IsAffine X]`, via transport of
73	  `isGaloisQuotient_spec` along the equivariant `X.isoSpec`. Measured both ways
74	  **from a file that imports that module** — the qualification is load-bearing and
75	  this file is two import hops *below* it, so neither claim can be reproduced here:
76	  `inferInstance` closes the goal at the formerly hand-built witness
77	  `hasGaloisQuotient_specF4`, and **fails** for an abstract `ρ` carrying the orbit
78	  hypothesis without affineness. So the remaining `G2(c)` work is the gluing of
79	  `Spec (A_U^Γ)` along a stable affine cover — the step the repaired
80	  representability route actually runs on, since its consumer `J'_r` is glued.
81	* `affineGaloisQuotientHomEquiv` — **the affine case of the Hom property, proved**:
82	  for `X' = Spec A` and affine `T = Spec B`,
83	  `Hom_{Spec K}(T, Spec A^Γ) ≃ Γ-invariant Hom_{Spec L}(T ×_K Spec L, Spec A)`,
84	  by Speiser descent (`SemilinearAlgebras.invariantAlgHomEquiv`) — never via
85	  Noether invariant finiteness.
86	
87	Campaign reference: `G2` of `informal/pic-representability-campaign.md` (consumed by
88	`G3`/`G4`; curve-agnostic, reusable for `Sym^d`/Albanese).  Sources: Milne, *Jacobian
89	Varieties* §4 and Kleiman, *The Picard scheme* (FGA explained) §4 use exactly this
90	finite Galois quotient to descend `Pic_{C_{k'}/k'}` to `k`; the affine heart is
91	Speiser's theorem.
92	-/

101	/-! ## Spec of a ring action -/
102	
103	section SpecAut
104	
105	variable (G : Type*) [Group G] (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [MulSemiringAction G A]
106	
107	lemma toRingHom_comp (γ τ : G) :
108	    (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A γ).comp (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A τ)
109	      = MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A (γ * τ) :=
110	  RingHom.ext fun x => (mul_smul γ τ x).symm
111	
112	lemma toRingHom_one : MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A (1 : G) = RingHom.id A :=
113	  RingHom.ext fun x => one_smul G x
114	
115	/-- A group acting on a commutative ring by ring automorphisms acts on `Spec A` by
116	scheme automorphisms: `γ` acts by `Spec (γ⁻¹ • ·)`.  The inversion is forced jointly
117	by the contravariance of `Spec` and the `Aut` group law, so that `toSpecAut` is a
118	group **homomorphism** (not an anti-homomorphism). -/
119	noncomputable def toSpecAut : G →* Aut (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) :=
120	  MonoidHom.mk'
121	    (fun γ =>
122	      { hom := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A γ⁻¹))
123	        inv := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A γ))
124	        hom_inv_id := by
125	          rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, toRingHom_comp,
126	            inv_mul_cancel, toRingHom_one, CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id]
127	        inv_hom_id := by
128	          rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, toRingHom_comp,
129	            mul_inv_cancel, toRingHom_one, CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id] })
130	    (fun γ τ => by
131	      refine Iso.ext ?_
132	      change Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A (γ * τ)⁻¹))
133	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A τ⁻¹)) ≫
134	          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A γ⁻¹))
135	      rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, toRingHom_comp, ← mul_inv_rev])
136	
137	lemma toSpecAut_hom (γ : G) :
138	    (toSpecAut G A γ).hom
139	      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G A γ⁻¹)) := rfl
140	
141	lemma toSpecAut_mul_hom (γ τ : G) :
142	    (toSpecAut G A (γ * τ)).hom = (toSpecAut G A τ).hom ≫ (toSpecAut G A γ).hom := by
143	  rw [map_mul]; rfl
144	
145	lemma toSpecAut_inv_hom (γ : G) :
146	    (toSpecAut G A γ⁻¹).hom = (toSpecAut G A γ).inv := by
147	  rw [map_inv]; rfl
148	
149	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
150	lemma toSpecAut_hom_inv_hom (γ : G) :
151	    (toSpecAut G A γ).hom ≫ (toSpecAut G A γ⁻¹).hom = 𝟙 _ := by
152	  rw [toSpecAut_inv_hom, Iso.hom_inv_id]
153	
154	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
155	lemma toSpecAut_inv_hom_hom (γ : G) :
156	    (toSpecAut G A γ⁻¹).hom ≫ (toSpecAut G A γ).hom = 𝟙 _ := by
157	  rw [toSpecAut_inv_hom, Iso.inv_hom_id]
158	
159	end SpecAut
